Recapping Port Milwaukee’s Big Year With Great Lakes Cruises

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:43
Instaread

The number of passengers nearly doubled from last year, showing major growth in the city’s ability to manage cruise lines.

BY Rich Rovito

Port Milwaukee welcomed nearly 20,000 passengers throughout its record-breaking 2026 cruise season, which ended Oct. 31.  

Port Milwaukee recorded 62 cruise ship calls among eight individual vessels, bringing 19,820 visitors to Milwaukee and the Great Lakes region. In 2025, Milwaukee received about 11,000 cruise passengers across 22 ship calls. Cruise lines serving Port Milwaukee in 2026 included American Cruise Lines, Pearl Seas, Ponant, Hapag Lloyd, Victory and Viking.  

The 2026 Great Lakes cruising season kicked off on April 23 with the arrival of the Viking Polaris and concluded with a visit by the American Patriot.  

“Milwaukee’s 2026 cruise season was another exciting opportunity to showcase our city to visitors from around the world,” Milwaukee Mayor Cavalier Johnson said in a statement. “Each ship docked along our shoreline brings visitors who support our local businesses and restaurants, and contributes to the vibrancy of our waterfront.”

Learn More

The 2026 season marked a milestone with the arrival of American Cruise Lines, which launched its Great Lakes itineraries through Port Milwaukee this season, further demonstrating the growing interest in Milwaukee as a destination and gateway to the Great Lakes.  

This season included nine occasions with two simultaneous cruise visits, as well as three dates when three cruise ships were in the city concurrently. On May 17, both the Viking Octantis and Viking Polaris docked at the heavy lift dock. This was the first time these sister vessels have shared a dock in Milwaukee, an operation that required extensive coordination between logistical, tourism and safety partners, according to Port Milwaukee.

“The 2026 season truly showed Port Milwaukee’s growing presence in the Great Lakes cruise industry,” Port Milwaukee Director Benji Timm said in a statement. “We are grateful to our cruise line partners, local tourism organizations and community stakeholders who helped make this season a success. With continued interest in Milwaukee as a cruise destination and the upcoming opening of our new South Shore cruise dock, Port Milwaukee is well positioned to create more opportunities for visitors to experience our city.” 

Port Milwaukee also shared an update concerning the construction of the new South Shore cruise dock, which it stated “remains on track and on budget” for completion by the end of this year, with a formal opening celebration scheduled to coincide with the first cruise ship arrival of the 2027 season, scheduled to take place on May 8 with the arrival of Viking Octantis.

Plans had initially called for the new dock to open during the 2026 cruise season, with Timm stating at a press conference in April that the South Shore dock would open in August.

“Due to the project’s complexity and factors outside Port Milwaukee’s control, the dock will welcome its first cruise ship at the start of the 2027 cruise season. This evolving timeline had no impact on the Port’s 2026 cruise operations,” a Port Milwaukee spokesperson said in a statement provided to Milwaukee Magazine.

The new dock is designed to accommodate the largest cruise ships operating on the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Seaway System, a 2,300-mile, bi-national, deep-draft waterway connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the upper Midwest, positioning Milwaukee to attract additional cruise activity.

The South Shore dock will offer a more welcoming site for arriving cruise passengers and will replace the city heavy lift dock on Jones Island, a gritty industrial location.

The planned May 8 start of the 2027 cruise season will be more than two weeks later than this year’s cruise season kick off.

A Port Milwaukee spokesperson told Milwaukee Magazine that the planned 2027 start is “nothing out of the ordinary,” noting that the 2026 start to the cruise season was earlier than usual.

Beyond infrastructure investments, several ongoing efforts remain underway to promote passenger cruise business in Milwaukee and throughout the Great Lakes.

Visit Milwaukee, Great Lakes Shore Excursions and various local stakeholders promote cruising activity in the city, working together to elevate Milwaukee’s visibility as a destination and strengthen the region’s position in the growing international cruise market, according to Port Milwaukee.

“This record-breaking season brought the world to Milwaukee, giving nearly 20,000 cruise visitors a chance to discover our incredible food, explore our neighborhoods, visit our cultural institutions and experience the hospitality that makes this city so memorable,” Visit Milwaukee President and CEO Peggy Williams-Smith said in a statement. “Those visits bring customers through the doors of our local businesses and introduce Milwaukee to new audiences around the globe.”

The 2025 cruise season created $2.5 million in local economic impact. Port Milwaukee officials previously stated that they expected this year’s figure to exceed $3.5 million. 

Additional data detailing the 2026 cruise season’s local economic impact is expected to be released at a later date.
